findings: Neet has broad triangular ears, projecting pale muzzle, fine supporting forelegs, full narrow seated trunk and a small rump nub; the coat reads smooth rather than engraved or shaggy.

Buddy has a continuous reclining trunk from neck through ribcage to folded haunch; paired forepaws bracket the ball and the rear paw belongs to the visible folded hind leg. Pale brows/muzzle, hanging ear flaps and dark torso retain identity in a close-groomed interpretation supported by B15.

Bone, remote and scattered balls make the imagined mission control readable. Buddy holds the removed ball at the sunny end of the rug; the contrasting upright commander and relaxed ball owner carry the joke.
Rug contact and cast shadows ground both animals. Furniture and floor perspective are coherent. No material anatomy, coat, support or finish defect found at native resolution.
Neet retains fine legs, connected full torso, large triangular ears and tiny nub. Four legs have legible ownership and floor contact; far-side overlap does not add limbs.

Buddy retains moderate torso elongation, neck, deep chest and substantial legs with clear abdominal clearance. Pale muzzle/brows and regional ear hair contrast with a close charcoal torso; fine wash variation does not create curls or raised shag.

The small flame narrows to the front lip at the open mouth below the black nose; the lowered jaw and visible oral opening establish mouth emission. It is intentional literal cartoon fire, as expressly stated in the story, not a photographic anatomy claim.

Buddy stands behind and watches open-mouthed, with an intact unsinged tail: this is the first flame before he edges closer. Green chutney cup, dosa and steel tableware supply the lunch context. The tight dining view omits other diners but does not contradict their off-frame presence.
Support shadows, continuous backs and floor perspective are coherent. The simplified close grooming is consistent across the selected images. No material visual defect found.
The toy has one round black plush body and six distinct dangling legs, three to each side. Neet grips its top edge with his mouth; the toy is neither floating nor confused with a dog limb.

Neet has four traceable legs in a moving stride, continuous neck/ribcage/pelvis, fine distal limbs and a tiny nub. Toy overlap is restricted to the muzzle and chest area. His smooth fawn coat has no etched curls or enlarged shag.

Buddy sits with two forepaws, two folded hind paws, supported haunches and an attached dark tapered tail. The close-groomed muzzle, pale brow arcs and hanging ears correspond to B15; the head remains connected to a substantial neck and chest.

Buddy is safely beside the doorway while Neet carries the oversized toy through the open lane. Their opposed activity levels carry the refusal-to-block-the-hall joke; the image is placed before the final collapse, so a walking/running carry is the correct state.
Floor contacts and shallow movement shadows are consistent with the stride. The hallway perspective connects to the home living area. No material identity, ownership, grooming or finish defect found.
